programmes.d: Fiona Bruce and team are in Belfast at the Parliament Buildings in Stormont Estate; an unloved muffin dish holds a surprise; Justin Croft spots an unread copy of "Ulysses"; John Foster delves into Belfast's 18th-century water system.
The most poignant items are chosen by the team to mark the end of World War I and its aftermath.

Fiona and the team return to the historic Abbey Pumping Station in Leicester; expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan swoons over some 1960s steel sculptures; books specialist Rupert Powell meets playwright Joe Orton's sister who brings in his typewriter.
The Antiques Roadshow looks back at some favorite finds from the past 40 years.
At Newcastle's Civic Center, Adam Schoon values a child's penny-farthing cycle; rare diaries tell the story of Victorian heroine Grace Darling and her mission to save lives at sea.
The Roadshow is in the elegant surroundings of Eltham Palace in south London.

The team returns for a second helping of finds from the Isle of Wight at Queen Victoria's Italianate seaside residence, Osborne; Richard Price challenges Fiona Bruce to work out how three clocks have changed in value since 1977.
Erddig in north Wales turns up some great surprises, including a ring from the Titanic.
A celebration of the outstanding achievements of some of Britain's most inspirational women, marking 100 years since women won the right to vote in 1918.
Crathes Castle in Aberdeenshire and its beautiful gardens host a Roadshow with a distinctly Scottish flavor.
The team presents from the Etaples Military Cemetery in France with a selection of emotive and poignant World War I items.
A goblet that survived the Great Fire of London is brought to Cromer seafront.
The team take a look back at some of the most memorable finds from the past 40 years, and what happened to the selection of items.
The team heads to Buckfast Abbey in Devon, currently commemorating 1,000 years of worship on the site.
Two unknown paintings by Diego Rivera; a collection of Gerry Anderson puppets.
This week, the Roadshow comes from the Concorde Hangar at the recently opened Aerospace Bristol museum.
An emerald and diamond ring worn on the Titanic; a fan's collection of James Bond props; a Welsh love spoon carved in 1859.
The Roadshow is in Piece Hall in Halifax, the only surviving 18th-century cloth hall.
Ornate silver from Iona; signed Harry Potter books; a unique Brooklyn Dodgers baseball; a German art deco figurine; an intricate Italian bracelet.
The Roadshow is at Wrest Park in Bedfordshire, a grand house built in the style of a French chateau.
At Cromer seafront in Norfolk, the experts uncover two pieces of exquisite Italian design; a Chinese vase bought from a London market turns out to be a very special find.
The Roadshow rolls into Manchester's Media City UK, home to some of Britain's best-loved TV.

The team are at historic Buckfast Abbey in Devon, commemorating 1,000 years of worship on the site; a tankard dating back to 1703; Adam Schoon shows how a hidden lock in a 1640s iron chest would deter thieves.
The Roadshow comes from the elegant surroundings of Eltham Palace, just a few miles from the heart of London.
Items range from an intricate model of a vintage car made by a prisoner of war to an Elizabethan ring found in a muddy field and even a collection of classic guitars.
At Crathes Castle in Aberdeenshire, treasures turn up that include a royal portrait that is not what it seems.

The team is in Yorkshire at Piece Hall in Halifax, the only surviving 18th-century cloth hall where textiles were once traded; treasures include a Chinese imperial robe, an opal pig and a sapphire brooch.
In Bristol, discoveries include a four-leaf clover brooch which brings luck to its owner.
A diamond and ruby pendant; an exotic and rare snuff container; a chair that once belonged to the Artful Dodger.
Fiona Bruce experts welcome thousands of visitors to Erddig in North Wales, the home of the Yorke family.
The show rolls into Manchester's MediaCityUK, home to some of Britain's best-loved television programmes, where Fiona Bruce meets "Blue Peter" presenters past and present.
The team is at Buckfast Abbey, a Benedictine monastery on the edge of Dartmoor in Devon.
At Eltham Palace in London, the team finds a pair of dueling pistols, a typewriter, and some of Winston Churchill's personal items.
The Roadshow is in Halifax, West Yorkshire, at the recently restored Georgian Piece Hall.
A Cartier clock; a tiny bowl with a giant price tag; and a royal portrait which is not all that it seems.
Wrest Park in Bedfordshire is the setting for today's roadshow.
A four-leaf clover brooch; a collection of Radiohead memorabilia; a former Concorde pilot talks about the celebrities he used to fly across the Atlantic.
The Roadshow is in Manchester at Media City UK, the site of the former Manchester docks.
A mourning ring connected to Charlotte Brontë; a Welsh love spoon handed down through the generations.
The Roadshow is in Norfolk, on Cromer's historic pier.
The team visits Buckfast Abbey, a Benedictine monastery in Devon, where they find a tiara, a mysterious teddy bear, and a silver platter.
The Roadshow is at the beautiful art deco Eltham Palace in south London.
A royal portrait by Beryl Cook and artwork by "Pennine Painter" Peter Brook; an art deco bracelet; a diamond necklace.
A selection of favourite finds from the past 25 years.
